title: Edge VPC: OTEL + Prometheus + Grafana deploy cheat sheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick operational cheat-sheet for deploying and upgrading the observability stack in VPC / on-prem edge sites. Focused on lightweight OTEL collector footprint, Prometheus scrape topology, Grafana provisioning, and safe Terraform-driven upgrades and rollbacks. This is intentionally terse — use as a runbook and checklist during rolling upgrades and on-call troubleshooting.

Context / constraints:
- Customers run Redwood Private in VPCs with limited egress.
- No external SaaS telemetry ingest allowed for some customers; logs must be egressed to S3/Kafka inside customer network or forwarded to a partner bridge.
- Need to support: Prometheus (ha optional), Grafana, OTEL collector (receiver -> processor -> exporter), Fluent Bit/Fluentd for logs.
- Must integrate with customer KMS for secrets and TLS certs.

High-level deployment patterns (decision checklist):
- Small edge (<= 8 nodes): single-replica Prometheus + sidecar remote_write to long-term store (if allowed) OR local TSDB with regular snapshots.
- Medium (8-64 nodes): Prometheus HA pair (replicated targets using different relabeling) + read-side Grafana backed by Loki or S3 logs.
- Large/regulated: Dedicated grafana stack with LDAP/SSO, multi-AZ Prometheus with Thanos/Querier for cross-site queries.

OTEL Collector pattern recommended (minimal footprint):
- Collector as DaemonSet on k8s or systemd unit on baremetal.
- Pipeline: receivers: otlp (grpc/http), prometheus_receiver (for k8s app metrics) -> processors: batch, memory_limiter, resourc e -> exporters: prometheusremotewrite (to internal ingestion) + file/forward (for debugging).
- Keep collector config modular: 
  - static_sinks/forwarders block per customer to toggle egress.
  - enable/disable kafka exporter via feature flag.

Sample OTEL snippet (plain text):
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
      http:
processors:
  batch:
  memory_limiter:
exporters:
  prometheusremotewrite:
    endpoint: https://ingest.internal.local/v1/metrics
service:
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp, prometheus]
      processors: [memory_limiter, batch]
      exporters: [prometheusremotewrite]

Prometheus scrape topology notes:
- Use relabeling to attach metadata (team, env, site) early in the scrape pipeline to keep metrics consistent across sites.
- Scrape job for node exporters and app pods should have a stable metric relabel_configs block. Example relabels: keep pod_namespace, replace target_label=site, add job_label from k8s label 'app'.
- For HA: run two Prometheus instances with different scrape intervals or stagger scrape targets (offset relabel) to reduce correlated load spikes.

Relabel example (text):
- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace]
  action: replace
  target_label: namespace

Grafana provisioning + dashboards:
- Use Grafana provisioning (files) checked into repo. Keep dashboard JSON in dashboards/ directory with versioned filenames.
- Have a small set of baseline dashboards: host-metrics, app-latency, otel-ingest-health, prometheus-tsdb-stats.
- Automate folder and data-source setup via terraform module that creates the Grafana org, datasources (Prometheus/Loki), and uploads dashboard snapshots.

Log shipping patterns:
- Prefer Fluent Bit as lightweight forwarder to customer internal Kafka or S3 gateway.
- When forwarding to S3: buffer on disk, use multipart uploads, enforce encryption with customer KMS.
- For high-throughput sites, use Fluentd on dedicated nodes to batch and compress logs before egress.

Terraform module notes (practical snippets):
- Keep modules small: module Prometheus (helm chart wrapper), module Grafana (helm + provisioning), module OTEL (daemonset/systemd), module FluentBit.
- Example module call (text):
module "prometheus" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-infra/tf-modules.git//prometheus?ref=main"
  namespace = "observability"
  helm_values = [file("../helm/prometheus-values.yaml")]
}
- Use separate workspaces per site to isolate state. Prefer remote state backend with encryption and per-site state key.
- For partial upgrades, use terraform apply -target=module.otel to change collector config without touching Prometheus. Avoid automations that rebuild PVCs for Prometheus unless intended.

Upgrade runbook (rolling upgrade recommended):
Pre-checks (20–60m)
- Verify Prometheus TSDB has snapshot/latest checkpoint. Run: curl -sS http://prom-svc:9090/api/v1/admin/tsdb/snapshot and store snapshot id in ticket.
- Ensure backups of PVCs (if supported) or export remote_write to long-term store.
- Validate alerting silence for noisy rules during upgrade window.
- Confirm helm/chart versions in git and terraform module refs.

Canary/rollout steps:
1) Deploy new OTEL collector config to one node/site with feature flag ON. Validate metrics flow to prometheusremotewrite and that ingestion rate is stable.
2) Apply Grafana provisioning change to non-prod folder first. Confirm dashboard renders.
3) Upgrade Prometheus Helm chart in a single replica (or non-primary) with paused scrape targets. Monitor TSDB size and compactions for 30–60m.
4) If Prometheus upgrade looks OK, proceed to HA partner, else rollback to previous helm chart.

Rollback steps (quick):
- If OTEL collector config causes drops: revert collector DaemonSet to prior revision (kubectl rollout undo).
- If Prometheus corrupted: stop new instance, restore from snapshot id using prometheus --storage.tsdb.path and copy snapshot.
- If terraform applied unintended resource replacement (PVC deletion): stop infra automation, state rm created resources, and follow restore PVC from backup procedure.

Monitoring of the upgrade (what to watch):
- Prometheus TSDB head series count, compactions, WAL size (prometheus_tsdb_head_series, prometheus_tsdb_wal_corruption_total).
- OTEL pipeline dropped metrics (otelcol_processor_drop_count).
- Ingestion latency and 95/99th p95/p99 scrape durations.
- Grafana datasource errors (500/403) and dashboard render failures.

Testing checklist after upgrade:
- Smoke: query host cpu, request latency for two apps, and verify dashboard panels render without missing data.
- Integrity: run series cardinality check against baseline; decrease is acceptable, increase likely indicates label explosion.
- Load: run synthetic scrape with -n 500 targets to see scrape controller behaviour under scale.

Security & secrets notes:
- Store TLS certs and KMS keys in customer-managed KMS; Terraform should support reading from KMS and not store raw certs in state. Use sops/encrypted values for non-KMS assets.
- Ensure OTEL grpc/http endpoints require mTLS when crossing trust boundaries.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Decide standard for snapshot retention policy per customer (default 7 days?).
- Should we offer a managed Thanos querier for cross-site queries in Dedicated contracts? (cost/complexity trade).
- Agreement with SRE on alert thresholds for TSDB compactions during upgrades.

Quick troubleshooting commands (k8s examples):
- Check collector logs: kubectl -n observability logs ds/otel-collector -f
- Snapshot Prometheus: curl -XPOST http://prom-svc:9090/api/v1/admin/tsdb/snapshot
- Grafana provisioning check: kubectl -n observability exec deploy/grafana -- grafana-cli admin --check-dashboards (internal script)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add a minimal terraform example for remote_write + s3 archiver and link to tf-modules repo.
- Draft a small playbook to teach on-call how to restore Prometheus from snapshot step-by-step with screenshots.
- Run a simulated upgrade weekend to validate rollback timing end-to-end.

Status: draft — please add comments for local site caveats (non-k8s installs, older kernel glibc issues) and tag any change that requires new customer permissions.
